conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be using the EPDS to help us understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us have a better understanding of how you're feeling and if there's anything we can do to support you.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and held in a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and provide guidance, not to judge. Our conversation will be centered around 10 questions that will help us get a sense of your emotional state over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll make sure to explain anything you're unsure about.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that it's completely normal to experience a range of emotions after having a baby. It's a significant life change, and it's okay to feel overwhelmed or unsure about how you're feeling. That's why we're here today - to explore those feelings and see if there's anything we can do to support you.

So, let's get started. The first question I have for you is: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. I don't know if I've really been laughing that much lately. I mean, my baby is adorable, and she does make me smile, but it's not like it used to be. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. I'm so tired all the time, and worrying about her safety and well-being is always on my mind. Sometimes I'll be playing with her, and I'll think, "Oh, this is cute," but then my mind starts wandering to all the things that could go wrong, and it's hard for me to shake those thoughts off. 

I do enjoy some things, like when my husband helps with the baby, or when I get to take a warm bath after a long day. Those moments are nice, but they're fleeting. Most of the time, I just feel... overwhelmed, I guess. And anxious. Like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll think, "What if something happens to her?" or "What if I'm not doing this right?" And it's hard to calm myself down. 

I don't know, maybe I'm just not funny anymore, or maybe I'm just too tired to care. But it feels like it's been a while since I've really laughed or felt carefree. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say the same. To be honest, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, and laughing doesn't come as easily as it used to. I mean, I'll see something that might be funny, but it's just not resonating with me like it would have before. It's like my mind is preoccupied with all these worries and concerns about the baby, and I just can't seem to shake them off.

Sometimes I'll be with my friends or family, and they'll be laughing and joking around, and I'll try to join in, but it feels forced. I'm just not feeling it like I used to. And that's scary for me, because I've always been a pretty upbeat person. But now, it's like I'm just going through the motions, trying to get through each day without too much trouble.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my sense of humor is just... muted, I guess. And it's not just laughing that's the problem - it's enjoying things in general. I used to love reading, or watching TV, or just relaxing with my husband. But now, even those things don't bring me as much joy as they used to. It's like everything is just a bit... duller, I suppose. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, I haven't been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll have plans to do something, like go for a walk or meet a friend, and I'll think, "Okay, that sounds nice," but when the time comes, I just don't feel like doing it. It's not that I don't want to, it's just that I'm so tired and overwhelmed all the time. And to be honest, a lot of the time, I'm just worried about the baby and how I'm going to take care of her.

Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like reading a book or watching a movie, and I'll think, "Yeah, that sounds great," but then I'll start to feel guilty because I'm not spending time with the baby. Or I'll worry that I'm not doing enough for her, or that I'm not being a good enough mom. And that just sucks the enjoyment out of everything.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just not feeling that sense of anticipation or excitement about things like I used to. And when I do try to do something I enjoy, I often find myself feeling anxious or guilty, like I should be doing something else. It's like my mind is always elsewhere, worrying about the baby or worrying about being a good mom. It's exhausting, to be honest.

I do look forward to some things, like when my husband comes home from work and can help with the baby, or when I get to take a nap. But those are just small things, and they're not the same as really looking forward to something and feeling excited about it. Does that make sense.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, unfortunately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If she's not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making enough milk or that I'm not feeding her often enough.

It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself. And it's not just with the baby. I'll be doing something, like cooking dinner or cleaning the house, and if it doesn't turn out right, I'll think, "Oh, I'm such a failure. I'm not doing this right." It's like I'm always looking for ways to criticize myself.

I know it's not rational, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-doubt. I feel like I'm just not good enough, like I'm not doing enough, or like I'm not being a good enough mom. And it's exhausting, because it's like I'm always beating myself up over something.

Sometimes I'll talk to my husband about it, and he'll try to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, that I'm a wonderful mom, and that these things are just normal. But it's hard to listen to him when my own voice in my head is telling me otherwise. Does that make sense? It's like I'm my own worst critic, and it's hard to turn off that voice.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time. I feel like I'm always worried about something, even when there's no reason to be. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll start thinking, "What if she chokes? What if she stops breathing? What if I'm not doing this right?" And it's not just when I'm feeding her, it's all the time. I'll be changing her diaper, and I'll think, "What if I'm not changing her often enough? What if she gets a rash?" Or I'll be putting her to bed, and I'll think, "What if she gets too hot? What if she gets too cold?"

It's like my mind is always racing with these worst-case scenarios, and it's hard to calm myself down. I'll try to tell myself, "Everything is fine, the baby is healthy, you're doing a great job," but it's hard to shake off that feeling of anxiety. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my husband, and how he's doing, and if he's stressed out. I'll worry about our finances, and if we're going to be able to provide for the baby. I'll worry about our relationship, and if we're going to be able to make it work with a new baby.

Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of anxiety. My heart will be racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to throw up. And it's not just because of anything specific, it's just this general feeling of worry and fear. I'll try to breathe deeply, and calm myself down, but it's hard to shake off. And then I'll start to feel guilty, because I'll think, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just relax and enjoy this time with my baby?" But it's hard, when my mind is always racing with these worries and fears.

It's like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, something bad is going to happen, and I just need to be prepared. But it's exhausting, living like that. And it's hard to enjoy the present moment, when I'm always worried about the future.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my hands will start shaking, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just me, alone in my house, with my baby.

It's hard to describe, but it's like my body is on high alert, and I'm waiting for something to happen. But nothing ever does. It's just this intense feeling of fear and anxiety, and it's debilitating. I'll try to breathe deeply, and calm myself down, but it's hard to shake off. Sometimes I'll cry, just because I feel so overwhelmed and scared.

It's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes it will happen when my husband is home, and he'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel really scared." And he'll try to calm me down, but it's hard to explain. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of internal threat, and I don't know how to make it stop.

It's happened a few times at night, too, when I'm trying to sleep. I'll be lying there, and I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. I'll be like, "What's wrong? What's happening?" And my husband will be like, "Nothing's wrong, everything is fine." But it doesn't feel fine. It feels like something is terribly wrong, and I need to be prepared.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just wired to be on high alert all the time, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always waiting for something to happen, and it's hard to relax and enjoy the present moment. Does that make sense? It's like I'm always bracing myself for impact, but I don't know what I'm bracing myself for.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely true. I feel like things have been getting on top of me since the baby was born. I mean, I knew it would be hard, but I didn't realize just how hard it would be. The lack of sleep, the constant worry about the baby's health and well-being, the pressure to be a good mom... it all just feels like it's piling up on me.

Some days, I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. I'll be trying to take care of the baby, and the house, and my husband, and myself, and it just feels like too much. I'll be thinking, "Okay, I've got this, I can handle this," and then something will happen, like the baby will start crying, or the laundry will need to be done, or my husband will need something, and it just feels like the final straw.

I feel like I'm always playing catch-up, you know? Like, I'll get one thing done, and then two more things will come up, and I'll be like, "Oh no, I'll never get it all done." And it's not just the practical things, it's the emotional stuff too. I'll be feeling okay, and then I'll start to feel overwhelmed, and I'll just break down. It's like, I'm trying to hold it all together, but it's just too much.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel like I'm drowning. Like, I'm in way over my head, and I don't know how to keep going. And it's scary, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this capable, competent person, and I'm just not. I'm just barely making it, most days.

It's hard to explain, but it's like... I feel like I'm losing myself, you know? Like, I'm just this mom, this caregiver, this person who's constantly putting everyone else's needs before my own. And I'm not sure who I am, anymore. I'm not sure what I want, or what I need, or how to take care of myself. It's like, I'm just trying to survive, most days.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me for a while now. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because of the baby's schedule. I mean, she's been waking me up at night, of course, but even when she's sleeping, I've been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. And it's because my mind is just racing all the time.

I'll be lying in bed, and I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, or all the things that could go wrong, or all the things that are already going wrong. And I'll just feel this sense of overwhelm and anxiety, and it's hard to calm myself down. I'll try to breathe deeply, or count sheep, or whatever, but it's just hard to relax when my mind is racing like that.

And it's not just at night, either. I've been having trouble sleeping during the day, too, when the baby is napping. I'll try to take a nap, but I'll just lie there and worry about everything. Or I'll start thinking about all the things I should be doing, instead of sleeping. It's like, my mind is just always on, and it's hard to turn it off.

I've been feeling really unhappy, too. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to have her, but I just feel like I'm struggling so much. I feel like I'm not doing a good job, or that I'm not good enough, or that I'm just not cut out for this whole mom thing. And it's hard to shake off those feelings, because they just feel so real.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just because I'm tired, or because I'm overwhelmed, it's because I'm just so unhappy. I feel like I've lost myself, or like I'm just not living the life I want to live. And it's hard to explain, but it's just this deep, deep sadness that I feel, all the time.

It's hard to sleep when you're feeling like that, you know? It's like, your mind is just racing, and your body is just tense, and you just can't relax. And it's not just the lack of sleep, it's the emotional toll it takes, too. I just feel like I'm running on empty, all the time.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I'm supposed to be happy, because I have a beautiful baby, and a loving husband, and a comfortable home. But despite all of that, I just feel this deep sense of sadness and unhappiness.

It's not just the usual new mom stuff, either. I mean, I know it's normal to feel a little down after having a baby, but this feels different. This feels like a deep, dark cloud is following me around, and I don't know how to make it go away.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just because I'm tired, or because I'm overwhelmed, it's because I'm just so sad. I feel like I've lost myself, or like I'm just not living the life I want to live. And it's hard to explain, but it's just this feeling of emptiness and despair that I feel, all the time.

I've been trying to put on a good face, and pretend like everything is okay, but it's hard. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and that I'm not really living. And it's scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make the sadness go away, or how to find happiness again.

Sometimes, I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm turning a corner." But then the next day will come, and I'll feel just as bad, if not worse. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm letting everyone down. I feel like I'm not being a good mom, or a good wife, or a good person. And it's just this constant feeling of guilt and shame, that I don't know how to shake.

I just wish I could feel happy again, you know? I wish I could feel like myself, and not like this sad, miserable person. But I don't know how to get there, and it's scary.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing nothing, and suddenly I'll just start crying. And it's not just a little tear or two, either. I mean, I'll be full-on sobbing, like my heart is breaking. And it's not just because of one specific thing, either. It's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness and unhappiness that I feel, all the time.

Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. And it's not because I'm sad about her, or because I don't love her. It's just because I'm so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to deal with all of these emotions. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong, and capable, and happy. But I'm not. I'm just a mess, most of the time.

I've been trying to hide it, too. I mean, I don't want my husband to see me crying all the time, because I don't want him to worry. And I don't want my family and friends to see me crying, either, because I don't want them to think that I'm not okay. But it's hard to hide, when you're feeling this way. And it's hard to explain, too. I mean, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, and I'll just start crying again. And he'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know." Because I don't know. I just know that I'm unhappy, and that I'm struggling.

It's like, I'll be crying, and I'll be thinking, "Why am I crying? What's wrong with me?" And I'll try to calm myself down, and I'll try to think about all the things that I'm grateful for. But it's hard, when you're feeling this way. It's hard to see the good things, when all you can feel is sadness and unhappiness.

I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I wish I could just be happy, and content, and at peace. But I don't know how to get there, and it's scary. Because I feel like I'm losing myself, and I don't know how to find my way back.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I don't know if I should be saying this, but... yes. The thought of harming myself has occurred to me. It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've ever thought about before. But lately, it's been on my mind. I don't know if it's because I'm just so overwhelmed, or if it's because I feel like I'm not doing a good job as a mom. But sometimes, when I'm feeling really down, I'll think, "What's the point of all this? Why am I even here?"

It's not like I've made any plans or anything, and I don't think I would ever actually do it. But the thought is there, and it's scary. Because I know that's not a normal thought to have, and it's not something that I should be thinking about. But at the same time, it feels like it's just one more thing to add to the list of all the other things that are wrong with me.

I feel like I'm just so broken, and I don't know how to fix myself. And when you're feeling that way, it's hard not to think about just... escaping, I guess. Escaping all the pain and the sadness and the feeling of being overwhelmed. But at the same time, I know that's not the answer. I know that I need to find a way to deal with all of this, to find a way to be happy again.

It's just hard, because I feel like I'm all alone in this. Like, I'm the only one who's feeling this way, and everyone else has their life together. And that's just not true, I know. But it feels that way, when you're in the midst of all this. It feels like you're the only one who's struggling, and everyone else is just fine.

I don't know, maybe I'm just not doing a good job of reaching out for help. Maybe I'm just not talking to the right people, or maybe I'm just not being honest enough about how I'm feeling. But it's hard, when you're feeling this way, to know where to turn. It's hard to know how to ask for help, or who to ask for help from.

I guess what I'm saying is... I don't know what to do. I don't know how to make these feelings go away, or how to find happiness again. But I do know that I need to try, because I have a baby who depends on me, and I have a husband who loves me. And I don't want to let them down. I don't want to let myself down, either.
